extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent attorneys/agents involved in drafting and prosecuting U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for the form, numbering, dependency, and examination of patent claims in U.S. applications, including rules for dependent and multiple dependent claims, fee calculation, and examiner practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claim alternative-only reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dependent claim which refers to more than one other claim (“multiple dependent claim”) shall refer to such other claims in the alternative only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multiple dependent claim shall not serve as a basis for any other multiple dependent claim. 35 U.S.C. 112(e) authorizes multiple dependent claims only in alternative form (e.g., “A machine according to claims 3 or 4, further comprising ---”). Cumulative claiming (e.g., “A machine according to claims 3 and 4, further comprising ---”) is not permitted. These limitations avoid undue confusion in determining how many prior claims are referred to in a multiple dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of dependent and multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in dependent form shall be construed to include all the limitations of the claim incorporated by reference into the dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multiple dependent claim shall be construed to incorporate by reference all the limitations of each of the particular claims in relation to which it is being considered. 35 U.S.C. 112 indicates that limitations of each claim incorporated into a multiple dependent claim must be considered separately—i.e., a multiple dependent claim does not contain all limitations of all alternative claims in any one embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee calculation for multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For fee calculation purposes under § 1.16, a multiple dependent claim will be considered to be that number of claims to which direct reference is made therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim depending from a multiple dependent claim will be considered to be that number of claims to which direct reference is made in that multiple dependent claim. An original application filed with or amended to include multiple dependent claims must have paid the fee set forth in § 1.16(j). Use form PTO/SB/07 together with PTO/SB/06 for fee computation; OPAP and TC technical support staff verify fees. If a multiple dependent claim is improper, OPAP may mark it; improper multiple dependent claim fee treatment and examples are provided (encircled numerals, counting rules, and example calculations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must conform to specification and have antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must conform to the invention as set forth in the remainder of the specification and the terms and phrases used in the claims must find clear support or antecedent basis in the description so that the meaning of the terms in the claims may be ascertainable by reference to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.58(a). Claims present on the filing date may be relied upon to establish disclosure if their content justifies it. If subject matter is claimed that is not shown in drawings or description but the claim itself is a clear disclosure, the claim should be treated on its merits and the drawing/description should be amended rather than objecting to the claim. However, if the claim does not provide its own description, it should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for failing to provide an adequate written description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-type independent claim structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the nature of the case admits, as in the case of an improvement, any independent claim should contain in the following order: (1) A preamble comprising a general description of all the elements or steps of the claimed combination which are conventional or known; (2) A phrase such as 'wherein the improvement comprises,' and (3) Those elements, steps, and/or relationships which constitute that portion of the claimed combination which the applicant considers as the new or improved portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form of claim required in 37 CFR 1.75(e) is intended for improvement-type inventions and is to be considered a combination claim. The preamble of this form is considered to positively and clearly include all elements recited therein as part of the claimed combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and assignment of claim numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The original numbering of the claims must be preserved throughout the prosecution. When claims are canceled the remaining claims must not be renumbered. When claims are added, they must be numbered by the applicant consecutively beginning with the number next following the highest numbered claim previously presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the application is ready for allowance, the examiner, if necessary, will renumber the claims consecutively in the order in which they appear or as requested by applicant. Form paragraph 6.17 may be used to notify applicant. In a single claim case, the claim is not numbered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and grouping of claims by scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The least restrictive claim should be presented as claim number 1, and all dependent claims should be grouped together with the claim or claims to which they refer to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should preferably be arranged in order of scope from broadest to most detailed. Where separate species are claimed, claims of like species should be grouped together where possible. Product and process claims should be separately grouped to facilitate classification and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims placement on separate sheet/page
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any sheet including a claim or portion of a claim may not contain any other parts of the application or other material. See ¶ 6.18.01 Claims: Placement (claims must commence on a separate sheet or electronic page per 37 CFR 1.52(b)(3) and 1.75(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line indentation / separation of claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim sets forth a plurality of elements or steps, each element or step of the claim should be separated by a line indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be plural indentations to further segregate subcombinations or related steps. In general, printed patent copies will follow the format used but printing difficulties may prevent duplication of unduly complex claim formats. See 37 CFR 1.75(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and formatting of reference characters in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters corresponding to elements recited in the detailed description and the drawings may be used in conjunction with the recitation of the same element or group of elements in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters should be enclosed within parentheses so as to avoid confusion with other numbers or characters which may appear in the claims. Generally, the presence or absence of such reference characters does not affect the scope of a claim. If reference characters are not enclosed within parentheses and that omission renders the claim indefinite, reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (use form paragraph 7.34.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required claim wording and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: While there is no set statutory form for claims, the present Office practice is to insist that each claim must be the object of a sentence starting with 'I (or we) claim,' 'The invention claimed is' (or the equivalent). Each claim begins with a capital letter and ends with a period. Periods may not be used elsewhere in the claims except for abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, at allowance, the quoted terminology is not present, it is inserted by the Office of Data Management. See Fressola v. Manbeck, 36 USPQ2d 1211 (D.D.C. 1995).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling duplicate or substantially duplicate claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims in an application comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(d) but are duplicates, or are so close in content that they both cover the same thing despite slight wording differences, it is proper after allowing one claim to object to the other claim under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of the allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.05.05 (warning) and 7.05.06 (duplicate claim objection) may be used. If duplicate claims are present but not allowable, use 7.05.05 to give applicant opportunity to correct. If duplicate claims are allowable, use 7.05.06. Examiner notes emphasize applicant's right to restate the invention in a reasonable number of ways and that mere difference in scope can be enough to justify restatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper dependent claim test (35 U.S.C. 112(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(d), a claim in dependent form shall contain: (i) a reference to a claim previously set forth, and (ii) then specify a further limitation of the subject matter claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dependent claim shall be construed to incorporate by reference all the limitations of the claim to which it refers. The test is that the dependent claim must include every limitation of the claim from which it depends and specify a further limitation. Example: if claim 1 recites A, B, C, D, a claim reciting claim 1 with D omitted or replaced by E would not be a proper dependent claim even if it places further limitations on the remaining elements. Dependent claims that fail these requirements should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(d) (use form paragraphs 7.36 and 7.36.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection (not mere objection) for non-compliant dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dependent claim does not comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(d), the examiner should reject the dependent claim under 35 U.S.C. 112(d) as unpatentable rather than objecting to the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(d) renders a dependent claim unpatentable just as non-compliance with other paragraphs of 35 U.S.C. 112 would. See Pfizer, Inc. v. Ranbaxy Labs., Ltd., 457 F.3d 1284 (Fed. Cir. 2006) (dependent claim invalid for failure to comply with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph). Use form paragraphs 7.36 and 7.36.01 to state statutory basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial fee-purpose treatment of dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial determination, for fee purposes, as to whether a claim is dependent must be made by persons other than examiners; it is necessary, at that time, to accept as dependent virtually every claim which refers to another claim, without determining whether a true dependent relationship exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial acceptance of a claim as a dependent claim does not preclude a subsequent holding by the examiner that a claim is not a proper dependent claim. TC technical support staff and OPAP handle initial fee calculations and marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable multiple dependent claim forms and common anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of unacceptable multiple dependent claim wording include: references that do not refer back in the alternative only (e.g., 'according to claim 3 and 4'), references to two sets of claims to different features (e.g., 'as in claim 1 or 4 made by the process of claims 5,6,7, or 8'), references to numerically following claims which are not understandable, and reference back to another multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific unacceptable examples are provided (e.g., 'A gadget according to claim 3 and 4, further comprising ---' or 'A gadget as in claims 1 or 2 and 7 or 8, which ---'). A multiple dependent claim may refer in the alternative to only one set of claims. A claim such as 'A device as in claims 1, 2, 3, or 4, made by a process of claims 5, 6, 7, or 8' is improper because 35 U.S.C. 112 allows reference to only a particular claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice for multiple dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For restriction purposes, each embodiment of a multiple dependent claim is considered in the same manner as a single dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, restriction may be required between embodiments of a multiple dependent claim. Some embodiments of a multiple dependent claim may be held withdrawn while other embodiments are considered on their merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling added/amended multiple dependent claims and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple dependent claims are added by amendment without the proper fee, the amendment should not be entered until the fee has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TC technical support staff verifies compliance with statute/rules and calculates additional fees using PTO/SB/07. If improper reference is noted in an added/ amended multiple dependent claim, a notation should be made in the left margin next to the claim and the numeral in the Dep. Claim column on PTO/SB/07 circled to call the matter to the examiner's attention. If multiple dependent claims are added and fees are insufficient, applicant/agent should be contacted to pay the additional fee; include a copy of the fee calculation form for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedures for claims referring to numerically following claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If any series of dependent claims contains a claim with an improper reference to a numerically following claim which cannot be understood, the claim referring to a following claim should normally be objected to and not treated on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where a claim refers to a numerically following claim and the dependency is clear both as presented and as it will be renumbered at issue, all claims should be examined on the merits and no form objection need be made; in such cases an examiner's amendment should be prepared if the order of the claims is changed. Any unusual problems should be brought to the supervisor's attention. Examples A and B illustrate both treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action clarity requirement for multiple dependent claim embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 132 require that each Office action make it explicitly clear what rejection, objection and/or requirement is applied to each claim embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying singular dependent claims which do not include a reference to a multiple dependent claim, reference should be made only to the number of the dependent claim. When identifying embodiments included within a multiple dependent claim, each embodiment should be identified by using the number of the claims involved, starting with the highest, as necessary. If all embodiments are subject to a common rejection/objection/requirement, reference may be made only to the number of the individual dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for claim informalities and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs are provided for common claim informalities and objections (e.g., ¶ 7.29.01 Claims Objected to, Minor Informalities; ¶ 7.29.02 Reference Characters Not Enclosed Within Parentheses; ¶ 7.29.03 Spacing of Lines; ¶ 7.45 Improper Multiple Dependent Claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.29.01 to point out minor informalities (spelling, inconsistent terminology) which should be corrected; if informalities render claims indefinite use form paragraph 7.34.01 to reject under 35 U.S.C. 112(b). Use 7.45 for improper multiple dependent claims (insert suggested bracketed language). Use 7.05.05/7.05.06 for duplicate claim warnings or objections.
